selected.rationale: Loss on the synchronous WebApp->Ordering.API checkout call can hang the order-placement request to the client deadline, exposing missing per-request timeout/retry on the most critical business path. The ordering edge is the core transaction and any availability failure directly blocks revenue.

Mobile checkout uses the same Ordering.API through a synchronous BFF call; loss here stalls the order flow and reveals whether the BFF/API has timeout/retry defense on the second primary front door. It is the mobile revenue path and an equally high-impact endpoint.

Delaying WebApp->Basket.API on the cart/checkout path propagates latency directly to the user and, without a bounded timeout or circuit breaker, becomes an unbounded checkout stall. This edge is the first step of the purchase flow and tests synchronous latency-handling.

Basket.API's state is in Redis; losing this edge breaks cart reads/writes and makes the whole basket/checkout flow unavailable. Expected weakness is missing fallback/degradation and automatic recovery for the cart state dependency.

Loss between Ordering.API and order-db prevents persisting new orders, turning a checkout success into a database-availability failure. This tests for missing retry, transaction fallback, and recovery at the most critical persistence boundary.

Dropping RabbitMQ traffic for OrderProcessor stalls order state progression indefinitely, exposing missing event retry/DLQ/outbox or consumer recovery. The async order pipeline becomes stuck without any automatic repair.

Losing payment events on PaymentProcessor->RabbitMQ can leave payments unrecorded and orders permanently in submitted state. This reveals missing reliable delivery (publisher confirms/retry/recovery) on the revenue-critical payment path.

Identity is a synchronous hard dependency for authentication; loss on WebApp->Identity.API can lock users out of the storefront with no fallback. Expected failure is missing timeout/degradation behavior on a security-critical edge.

Loss on the primary catalog browse edge makes the storefront product page fail immediately; if no timeout/cache fallback exists, the outage is visible to every user. It validates read-path resilience on a high-traffic synchronous call.

Ordering.API's integration events to RabbitMQ drive downstream order state; network loss here silently desynchronizes order lifecycle across services. The weakness would be missing publisher confirm/retry/outbox on the event bus.
